approach: Add one reading-acceptance check, `check_scope_limit` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, with one `step!(check_scope_limit(reading));` line in `refusing_check` after `check_defined_terms` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It reuses the matcher that already decides enforcement, `athena_context::briefs::limits_changed_files` (briefs.rs:146); at verification that matcher makes the deliverable list the allowlist (`allowed_paths`, briefs.rs:115). Root cause: nothing at the reading gate compares a scope limit with the files Athena always writes (CHANGELOG.md) or with the readers of a changed config, so a limit written from the named files passes the gate and later fails verification (class scope-criterion-too-narrow-misses-dependent-tests; jobs 20261018-045437-7z81 and 20261023-052543-9bw7). Two refusals: (1) a limiting criterion that names a file must also name CHANGELOG.md or point to 'the deliverables'; (2) when a limiting criterion exists and athena.toml or defaults.toml is a deliverable, the reading must list a crates/ test deliverable or carry a `Consumers:` assumption naming a crates/ path. Matching is mechanical, with no repo content scan. Support work: one line in `READING_RULES`; unit tests in reading.rs; corpus cases with new input-form tags; a one-constant fix to the scope-test fixture `LIMIT` in run/tests.rs (forced: the fake reader pushes it through the real gate); a CHANGELOG entry; decision D166. Revision round 2: demonstration 6 now sets fails_without and seam; run/tests.rs is justified (decision 6) and raised as a User question.

decisions.choice: The CHANGELOG.md rule reads the limiting criterion's text: it must name CHANGELOG.md or the word 'deliverable'. A CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not repair the limit.
decisions.reason: `build_reading` calls `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:859; definition 297-319) before `check_reading_acceptance` (reading.rs:680), so every change reading already lists CHANGELOG.md when the gate runs. A rule that accepted 'CHANGELOG.md listed' would never fire in production. The 9bw7 failure was a limit sentence that omitted the file. This departs from the wording of criterion 2 ('with CHANGELOG.md listed'); the unit test shows both the literal form and the production form.

rejected.option: Accept when CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable (the literal reading)
rejected.why: Inert for every production reading, so the class would stay open.

rejected.option: Refuse a limit unless it lists every deliverable by name
rejected.why: Larger refusal rate than the evidence supports; 'the deliverables' is the existing way to point at the list.

decisions.choice: A scope limit is a criterion for which `limits_changed_files` is true. out_of_scope items are not scanned. The CHANGELOG half fires only when the limit text names a file (a word with '/' or a name.ext with an extension of at least 2 characters).
decisions.reason: One definition for the gate and for verification-time enforcement (`limiting_criterion` reads criteria only, briefs.rs:103-108), so the gate cannot drift from what is enforced. out_of_scope items are exclusions, never an allowlist. Departs from the reading's 'criterion or out_of_scope item'. 'No other file is changed' and 'production unchanged' name no file and are not refused.

rejected.option: A new phrase list ('only', 'nothing else', 'no other') in checks.rs
rejected.why: A second matcher that would drift from `limits_changed_files`; a broad 'only' also refuses sentences that limit nothing.
Enforcement ignores them, and exclusions such as 'files kept from job X' would cause false refusals.

decisions.choice: The config-consumer rule fires only with a limiting criterion and a deliverable named athena.toml or defaults.toml. It is met by a crates/ test deliverable (path under crates/ with a `/tests/` directory, or a file stem starting or ending with test/tests) or by an assumption starting `Consumers:` (any case, trimmed) that names a crates/ path (reuse `names_crates_path`, surveys.rs:127).
decisions.reason: With a limit the deliverable list is the allowlist, so an unlisted test that loads the real config fails the scope guard (what happened in 20261018-045437-7z81). Without a limit a producer may touch consumers freely. The `Consumers:` label mirrors `Code survey:` (surveys.rs:116-134). The check forces the question; it cannot verify the search, and D166 says so.

rejected.option: Scan the repo content for files that load the config
rejected.why: Out of scope; readers see a plain copy and the gate must stay deterministic.

rejected.option: Require the consumer rule for every config deliverable, even without a limit
rejected.why: Refuses readings that cannot suffer the failure.
check_governance_coverage already ties it to athena.toml through GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE (checks.rs:559).

decisions.choice: Default-written files go in a small const table (one row today: CHANGELOG.md with its reason), beside the config-file list, in checks.rs.
decisions.reason: Follows the table convention of GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE; the reason text feeds the error; a future default file is one row.

rejected.option: Hard-code the string CHANGELOG.md in the logic
rejected.why: Loses the 'why' for the error text and blocks a second file.
